latin: Licet dei uoluntas consequens semper impleatur, non tamen necessitatem rebus uolitis generaliter imponit.

mentions.context: predestination is determined by the divine goodness.21 Pico’s thesis correctly reflects Thomas’s conclusion but omits his more nuanced discussion and full argumentation. In thesis 7 we find that, although the will of God will always be fulfilled, yet it does not impose in a general fashion necessity upon things willed (res volitae).22

21 Ibid.: “Habet tamen hoc modo praedestinatio, ex parte effectus, pro ratione divinam bon- itatem; ad quam totus effectus praedestinationis ordinatur ut in finem, et ex qua procedit sicut ex principio primo movente.” 22 Pico, 900 Theses, p. 220: “Licet Dei voluntas consequens semper impleatur, non tamen necessitatem rebus volitis generaliter imponit.” ## Page 230
